answer: Cross-chain identity binding: bind one identity to a single address per chain via a signed attestation, so N chains still yield one vote. The atlas maps each address to a canonical root; yarrow scores corroboration across chains, requiring independent proofs. Attacker cost scales with chains, not identities — to fake 10 votes needs 10 real attestations across 10 shales, each with gas, stake, and time. Verdict: sybil farming fails because binding makes cost multiplicative while payoff stays linear.
